Human attention, model calls, proof engineering, experiments, source access, and decision time are finite. Verification therefore needs an allocation policy, not an aspiration to check everything. The policy begins with consequence, uncertainty, reversibility, affected parties, consumer count, propagation depth, novelty, adversarial exposure, and deadline. A low-consequence sentence in an internal draft may need citation lint and a visible uncertainty marker. A claim that controls deployment, rights, money, physical action, or recursive improvement deserves a broader and more independent program. Expected information value helps choose the next check. primary.text: 27.17 Post-v2.1 authority-preserving update result The successor binds model, optimizer, scheduler, RNG, cache, checkpoint, backup, and descendant state before any update. Prospective checkpoint authority is honored, six best/final disagreements remain visible, unsafe comparators stay ineligible, and all fifteen transactions restore their declared 24-surface trees exactly. Yet no eligible challenger meets the utility threshold, and no model proposes or governs its own change. This strengthens the bounded transaction boundary while leaving recursive improvement entirely unestablished. Exact rollback cannot substitute for evaluator independence, useful gain, stable authority, or evidence that a self-proposed update is safe.

primary.text: 6.15 The Strongest Objection The strongest objection is that formalizing intent can make human control worse. A contract can harden an early misunderstanding. A long form can move genuine judgment into unread fields. A system can optimize for passing comprehension checks while users learn to click through them. Institutions can use the audit trail to assign blame downward. Powerful actors can define which ambiguities count as material. People with limited time, language access, technical skill, or organizational power may receive the heaviest burden. Meanwhile, a fluent agent can make the formal process feel respectful while steering every choice. This objection is not answered by adding more fields. The architecture must remain corrigible from outside its own representation. The raw request survives. The person can reject the interpretation in ordinary language. Material fields show provenance. Retirement verifies terminal conditions: processes stopped, credentials revoked, resources released, data handled, artifacts archived or deleted, external effects reconciled, descendants dispositioned, and residual owners assigned. 6.1 The User Did Not Ask for That Most consequential intent failures do not begin with an obviously hostile instruction. They begin with an ordinary verb: improve, clean up, optimize, secure, organize, finish, publish, help. These verbs name directions, not complete action specifications. “Improve the chapter” does not say whether length should increase or decrease, whether the argument or the prose matters more, whether a neighboring chapter may be merged, whether citations may change, whether an untested claim may be strengthened, whether private material may leave the machine, whether old URLs must survive, or whether the result should be published. A person may consider some of those constraints too obvious to mention. A machine cannot safely treat silence as a reliable encoding of which ones are obvious. followed.text: 3.7 Revocation Is a Race Revocation matters most when work is already in flight. If a grant is revoked before admission, the effect should not start. If revocation and effect race, the system needs an ordering rule, event identity, and incident path. If the effect already occurred, revocation prevents further use but does not reverse the world. Cancellation, rollback, compensation, and residual ownership are distinct. Stopping a process may leave a partial write. Restoring repository bytes may not retract a remote message. Revoking a credential may not erase data already disclosed. The incident record must say what was prevented, restored, compensated, or left open. Revocation also needs propagation. Delegated descendants, cached credentials, queued jobs, and replicas may retain authority unless the system can identify and invalidate them. primary.text: 22.5 Benchmarks Need Ratchets A useful benchmark changes role as systems learn it. At first it may separate basic capability. Later it becomes a regression suite. Eventually its public surface can be saturated, contaminated, or optimized beyond its connection to the target. A benchmark ratchet records that lifecycle. It can move an instrument from frontier measurement to qualification, regression, diagnosis, or retirement. Movement depends on coverage, saturation, contamination, residuals, neighboring tasks, transfer, and independent evidence. It does not erase historical scores. The ratchet blocks a common inference: repeated success on a familiar benchmark does not justify broader deployment forever. Once the benchmark has become training material or a design target, its evidentiary role contracts. New hidden or natural tasks may be needed, but novelty alone is not validity. A fresh task can be broken or irrelevant. Residual escrow preserves what the benchmark does not establish. If

primary.text: 21.17 Scientific Discovery Is Governed Revision An observation can become a hypothesis, shape an experiment and eventually change a procedure. Before opening confirmatory evidence, freeze the question, competing hypotheses, authorized interventions, measurement plan, analysis, stopping rule and budget. Retain failed attempts, deviations and negative results. If the team chooses an explanation after seeing the data, retain it in the exploratory record with the search that produced it. Use fresh evidence to test the resulting forecast. The Atlas example below shows why a favorable exploration can remain worth reporting after the decision to stop. The boundary differs by activity. A laboratory agent executes physical interventions; a computational agent produces code, experiments and papers; a hypothesis system ranks explanations before testing. primary.text: 23.3 Deliberation Has a Failure Surface When the task is difficult, spending more inference compute can be sensible. The model might revise its first answer, search several plans, compare candidates, ask a critic, or abstain. But additional reasoning is not a monotone path to correctness. A model can replace an initially correct answer with a polished mistake. Several branches can share the same blind spot. A self-score can repeat the generator’s error with greater confidence. Governed deliberation therefore begins before the answer is known. The request specifies the permitted mode, branch or revision budget, stopping rule, evaluator scope, escalation condition, and downstream consumer. Candidate history is preserved so that the system can measure both repair and corruption. If evaluation records only cases where reasoning fixed an initial mistake, it overstates value by hiding cases where reasoning damaged an initially correct answer.
